note: Curated LLM-evaluation methodology tips, one per day, rotated by date. Add entries; keep titles short and bodies one paragraph.

tips.title: Chance level is a baseline, not a footnote
tips.body: Always run a random baseline (pocket-eval: `--backend random`). If a model scores at or below the coin flip, nothing in your pipeline is measuring knowledge.

tips.title: A lexical baseline shows what counting buys
tips.body: An n-gram model over your corpus is the cheapest known answer. Models that cannot beat it on definitional trivia are not 'thinking' — they are re-emitting training statistics.

tips.title: One run is a rumor
tips.body: LLM evaluation is noisy: sampling, tie-breaking and batching shift scores. Report seeds, repeat runs, and treat single-run numbers as anecdotes, not evidence.

tips.title: Perplexity is a fluency meter, not a reasoning meter
tips.body: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts tokens. Tiny models can score low perplexity on memorized text yet fail every reasoning question; report both.

tips.title: Leakage is the silent inflator
tips.body: If benchmark text appears in pretraining data, scores are rent, not capability. Write your own items (this repo's mini-benchmark is original) or check overlap first.

tips.title: Contamination corrupts comparisons
tips.body: Comparing model A on a benchmark B already saw in training is unfair. Keep a held-out set nobody shipped, and re-derive it when models get refreshed.

tips.title: Tokenization is part of the model
tips.body: BPE boundaries change what a prompt means to the model. 'erc 20' tokenizes differently than 'erc-20' — normalize inputs the same way for every model you compare.

tips.title: Short options inflate accuracy
tips.body: With 4 short options, a model can win by pattern-matching surface form. Vary option length and distractors or you will measure format, not understanding.

tips.title: Score, then squint
tips.body: Look at per-item scores, not just accuracy. Flat scores near zero mean the model cannot discriminate options at all — that is a finding, and it explains the accuracy.

tips.title: Match the prompt format to the model family
tips.body: Instruct-tuned models expect chat templates; base models expect raw text. Scoring with the wrong format degrades every number you publish.

tips.title: Determinism is a feature of harnesses
tips.body: Same model + same seed + same input must give the same report. If your eval is not bit-reproducible, regressions are invisible and comparisons are marketing.

tips.title: Bound the runtime dependency
tips.body: An eval that needs a GPU or an API key cannot run in CI, so it never runs. Keep a deterministic offline baseline in the default path — it is your regression gate.

tips.title: Benchmarks rot; corpora rot
tips.body: Domain language changes ('NFT', 'L2', 'AA') and models absorb old benchmarks. Refresh the corpus and the item set on a calendar, not when someone remembers.

tips.title: Sample size tells you what to believe
tips.body: The difference between 8/12 and 10/12 on one mini-benchmark is weak evidence. Scale items to 100+ before claiming a model is better; use the mini version to sanity-check pipelines.

tips.title: Report the floor and the ceiling
tips.body: Random chance (floor) and the lexical baseline (cheap ceiling) bracket every model score. Publish all three; a score without context is a headline, not a result.

tips.title: Human review is the terminal test
tips.body: Automated metrics miss the label errors, ambiguous items and tricks. Every release, hand-audit a sample of items and a sample of model answers.

tips.title: Regression gates belong in CI
tips.body: Pin golden numbers (this repo's tests do) so a dependency bump or a data edit that silently changes scores fails the build instead of drifting.

tips.title: Domain corpora must be original
tips.body: Scraping blog posts into an eval corpus imports license and leakage baggage. Write your own domain text; it costs an afternoon and pays in trust.

tips.title: Small models are probe assets
tips.body: A 15M-parameter model is worthless as a capability claim and invaluable as a harness validator: it should run in seconds on the same CPU you develop on.

tips.title: Log the exact inputs
tips.body: Store tokenized prompts, option order and seeds with every report. You cannot debug a score you cannot reconstruct, and you will need to reconstruct it.

tips.title: Accuracy is one axis; cost and latency are the other two
tips.body: A 3-point accuracy gain that triples latency may be a regression in production. Fold wall-clock time and peak memory into the leaderboard.

tips.title: Define the decision before you measure
tips.body: 'Which model deploys?' needs a threshold ('must beat the ngram baseline by 20 points on definitional items'). Metrics without decision rules get argued, not used.

tips.title: Version your eval
tips.body: Pin the harness version, corpus hash and benchmark version in the report header. 'It scored 83%' means nothing without the eval's own version stamp.

tips.title: The best eval is boring
tips.body: No surprise regressions, no leaked hints, reproducible in CI, one command. Glamour belongs in the model; rigor belongs in the harness.
